transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been a little worried about my eating lately. It’s not, like, all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but after really long days on site or after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and sort of… eat way more than I meant to.

Like whatever’s around—leftover takeout, cereal, chips—and then I end up feeling uncomfortably full. I just thought maybe I should bring it up and see if that’s something worth talking about.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset when you eat more than you meant to?

I mean… maybe stressed, yeah, but I’m not totally sure which comes first. It’s usually after I’ve had a long day or I’m kind of wound up, and then I eat more than I planned. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, extremely upset every time or anything… but I do feel uncomfortable and kind of disappointed in myself afterward, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during those times?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the part that worries me. I don’t want to make it sound like I have no control ever, but on those evenings, once I start, it kind of feels like I’m on autopilot.

I’ll be telling myself, okay, stop, you have an early crew start tomorrow, you need to go to bed… and then I still end up going back to the kitchen for more. It feels embarrassing to say, but yes, in those moments it’s harder to stop than I think it should be.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating more than you planned?

I mean… guilty might be a strong word? Maybe a little, sometimes. I mostly feel kind of annoyed with myself, like, “Why did I do that when I was trying to be reasonable?” But I don’t know if I’d call it guilt exactly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you're eating very quickly during those times when you can't stop?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to the speed of it. It doesn’t feel like I’m, you know, shoveling food down or anything… but maybe I’m eating faster than I normally would. I’d have to notice it more, if that’s okay.
Do you feel like you've lost control over your eating during those times when you eat more than you planned?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t love how that sounds, but on those evenings, once I start, it really can feel like I’m kind of on autopilot.

Like I’ll be telling myself, “Just stop, you’ve got an early crew start tomorrow,” and then I still end up back in the kitchen getting more. So… yes, I guess that does feel like losing control, at least in those moments.
Do you have times when you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s kind of what made me bring it up.

After a really long day on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll get home and just… eat way more than I meant to. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips, whatever’s around. And it can happen pretty quickly, I guess, enough that I end up uncomfortably full. Is that what you mean by a large amount?
Do you feel ashamed of yourself after these episodes of eating more than you planned?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it ashamed exactly. I mean, I definitely don’t feel great afterward. I usually feel kind of embarrassed with myself, like, “Why did I do that?” But I also try not to make a huge deal out of it, if that makes sense.

I guess… maybe a little ashamed, but I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these episodes of feeling like you're on autopilot while eating happen often?

Um… often enough that I probably shouldn’t pretend it’s rare.

If I look back over the last few months, I’d say it averages out to about once a week. Some weeks it might happen twice, and then other weeks not at all, so it’s not like every day or anything. But… yeah, weekly-ish is probably the honest answer.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Not really significant, I don’t think. My weight kind of goes up and down a little like it always has, but I haven’t noticed some big change or anything. At least nothing that made me think, “Oh, that’s different.” Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think you're eating more quickly than usual during those times when you feel like you're on autopilot?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really paid close attention to the speed, honestly. It feels more like I’m not fully thinking about it, if that makes sense, but I couldn’t say for sure that I’m eating faster than normal.

Maybe a little sometimes, but I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong answer.
Do you usually eat a large amount of food when you're feeling stressed or anxious?

Yeah… I mean, not every time I’m stressed, but that is kind of what made me bring it up.

After a really long day on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll get home and it’s like I just start eating whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips—and then I realize I’ve eaten way more than I meant to. Sometimes to the point where I’m uncomfortably full, which… I know doesn’t sound great.
Do you think you are eating rapidly during these episodes when you feel like you're on autopilot?

I honestly don’t know. It feels kind of embarrassing to say, but I’m usually not paying attention closely enough to know if I’m eating rapidly. It’s more like I zone out and then realize what happened after.

I mean, maybe I am sometimes, but I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not totally sure. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think you are eating rapidly during these episodes?

I’m sorry, I still don’t really know. I haven’t noticed the speed as much as the zoning-out part. I don’t want to say yes just because it sounds like that might fit… but I can try to pay attention to it more if that would help.
Do you think you are eating more food in a short amount of time, like within a couple of minutes, during these episodes?

I’m not sure it’s within just a couple of minutes… I don’t want to exaggerate it. But yes, the part that worries me is that after some really long days on site, or after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and eat way more than I meant to—like leftover takeout, cereal, chips, just whatever’s there—until I’m uncomfortably full.
Do you feel a sense of pleasure or a high during these episodes when you're eating more than you planned?

I don’t know if I’d call it pleasure or a high, exactly. Maybe there’s a little relief at first, like I’m finally not thinking about everything for a minute, but I haven’t really noticed feeling… good, exactly. It’s more complicated than that, I guess. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you're unable to control what or how much you're eating during those times when you're on autopilot?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. I don’t like admitting that, but on those evenings once I start, it’s like I’m kind of on autopilot. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, stop, you have an early crew start tomorrow,” and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more anyway. It’s not every time I eat or anything, but when it happens, it does feel hard to control.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating more than you planned?

I’m… not totally sure. I mean, I don’t feel great afterward, obviously, and I’ll usually think, “Why did I do that?” But I don’t know if I’d call it guilt every time. Maybe more embarrassed with myself, or frustrated. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel like you're not interested in eating?
I don’t think so… not usually. I mean, I might put off eating if I’m busy or stressed, but I wouldn’t say I’m just not interested in food in general. Is that what you mean?
Do you often go for long periods of time without feeling hungry?

I don’t think so, not long periods exactly. I mean, if I’m on a job site and things are hectic, I can sort of ignore it for a while, but I wouldn’t say I just don’t feel hungry for a long time. At least, I haven’t really noticed that. Is that okay—does that answer what you’re asking?
